hero.purpose: Today's headline on desktop, and nothing else. Steps to Headline at phone width.

headline.purpose: A page's h1; Today's headline on a phone.

title.purpose: A section title large enough to open a page region.

body.purpose: Every row title, task, and list item.

section.purpose: A section heading. Body size — the weight step to 500 is the entire signal.

meta.purpose: Clock times, counts, streaks, ruler hours. Always tabular.

eyebrow.purpose: Anything the system labelled rather than a person named — the dateline, ALL DAY, a bucket name.

micro.purpose: The one step below the ramp, in exactly three density-pressured mono sites: the day tape's per-block start times, the tape's ruler at phone width, and the dock's five tab labels at 375pt.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: Cards, panels, the active tab pill. Enough to separate paper from ground, not enough to read as a stack.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and the dock. Deeper on purpose — the dock floats over white cards and has to stay a separate object.

shadows.name: priority-halo
shadows.purpose: Around a high-priority checkbox. The only shadow carrying meaning rather than height.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: The day tape's assembly — blocks wipe out from their start edge, the now-mark drops in last.

motion.name: duration-dim
motion.purpose: The day-owned payload dimming while a day step is pending.

components.name: Capture Pill
components.description: The shell's primary action. Ink-filled because capture is the one action the product exists to make cheap.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 40px; padding: 0 20px; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--ink, #2a2524); color: var(--bg, #fafafa); font-family: Geist, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #f15a0f); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ask Pill
components.description: The quiet half of the shell's action pair. A hairline outline carrying full ink.

components.name: Control Button
components.description: The quiet mono voice the rest of the app is built from: row actions, form buttons, filters.

components.name: Tab Group
components.description: The desktop header's segmented pill. The active tab lifts onto paper; the rest sit quiet in the trough.
components.html: TodayTasksNotes

components.name: Priority Checkbox
components.description: The most-repeated shape on the page. Priority is a ring on the box, because the signal sits on the thing you reach for.
components.css: .ds-checks { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 18px; } .ds-check { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 19px; height: 19px; border: 1.5px solid var(--line-strong, #d6d3d0); border-radius: 7px; background: var(--surface, #fff); } .ds-check-p1 { border-width: 2px; border-color: var(--priority-high, #d92d20); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3.5px rgba(217,45,32,0.16); } .ds-check-p2 { border-width: 2px; border-color: rgba(217,45,32,0.42); } .ds-check-on { background: var(--ink, #2a2524); border-color: var(--ink, #2a2524); color: var(--surface, #fff); }

components.name: Day Tape
components.description: The signature. A pinned 06:00-22:00 measure: filled blocks are events, an outlined tick is a scheduled task, and the now-mark carries its own hour.
components.html: 06:0013:1022:00
components.css: .ds-tape { width: 100%; } .ds-track { position: relative; height: 46px; border-radius: 12px; background: var(--surface-2, #f0efed); } .ds-blk { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; min-width: 7px; border-radius: 8px; } .ds-blk-task { background: transparent; border: 2px solid currentColor; min-width: 9px; width: 0; } .ds-now { position: absolute; top: -6px; bottom: -6px; width: 2px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--ink, #2a2524); z-index: 3; } .ds-ticks { position: relative; height: 16px; margin-top: 9px; } .ds-ticks > span { position: absolute; transform: translateX(-50%); font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 12px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--ink-4, #b4aea8); } .ds-ticks > span:first-child { transform: none; } .ds-ticks .ds-end { left: auto; right: 0; transform: none; } .ds-ticks .ds-now-label { color: var(--ink, #2a2524); font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Completion Ring
components.description: One completion figure, drawn as a conic arc with an opaque punched centre that carries its own reading.
components.css: .ds-ring { position: relative; display: grid; place-items: center; width: 52px; height: 52px; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-hole { position: absolute; inset: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--surface, #fff); } .ds-val { position: relative; font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 12px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--ink-2, #57534e); }

components.name: All-day Chip
components.description: Everything that belongs to the day but has no hour. Chips wrap rather than scroll — a hidden chip is a missed commitment.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 30px; padding: 0 13px; border: 1px solid var(--line-strong, #d6d3d0); border-radius: 12px; font-family: Geist, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: var(--ink, #2a2524); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-dot { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 9999px; flex-shrink: 0; }

components.name: Field
components.description: No box and no radius — a transparent field over a single bottom rule.
components.css: .ds-field { display: block; } .ds-field-label { display: block; font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-3, #8c8681); } .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 36px; padding: 0 10px; border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, #e5e5e5); border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--ink, #2a2524); font-family: Geist, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #f15a0f); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Mobile Dock
components.description: The header's tabs moved to the thumb. The active tab takes the ember wash; capture takes ink. Two signals that can never be read as one.

narrative.overview:
Dispatch is one person's instrument for finding out what today is, and the system is built around a single act: measuring. The day tape measures committed time against free time. A ring measures routines done against routines left. A counter measures what is open against what is late. Everything else — the paper-white ground, the warm stone ink, the one orange — exists to keep those measurements legible, and nothing on a page is allowed to compete with them.

Type and colour are lifted from bydefault.so exactly, and geometry from collectiveos: Geist Sans at two weights only, a 56/44/36/30/18/16/14/12 ramp, a neutral-50 ground under a warm stone ink ladder, one orange accent, and large soft-cornered cards on a gentle lift. Hierarchy comes from size and colour and never from weight, because there is no weight above 500 to reach for. The result is quiet without being cold: the warmth is in the greys, not in decoration.

Three visual worlds have been rejected before this one, and each rejection is load-bearing. An editorial identity (warm linen, terracotta, a serif display face) was replaced. A fully monochrome restyle was rejected for being colourless. The Vercel/Geist system that followed — near-black canvas, Signal Blue, 600-weight display type, a mesh-gradient wordmark — is the immediate predecessor and the direct anti-reference for this one: revision A is light-first, is 500 at its heaviest, and has no gradient anywhere.
keyCharacteristics: Light by default; dark is a complete peer, not an afterthought
One orange, and it means exactly one thing: this needs you
Nine measured domain colours, which are data — never decoration
Large radii and a soft warm lift; hairlines still do the dividing
Shape distinguishes kinds; colour distinguishes instances

rules.name: The One Orange Rule
rules.body: The accent means "this needs you" and nothing else. Overdue, late, starred, focused. It is never a decoration, never a heading colour, and never used to make a section look important. If two things on a screen are orange for different reasons, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Measured Palette Rule
rules.body: Domain colours are data. They are generated and measured in .impeccable/mocks/palette-lab.html against three floors. Retune them in the lab and re-measure, or not at all — never by hand, and never one at a time.

rules.name: The Stored Slug Rule
rules.body: A domain's colour is stored as a palette slug (health), never as a hex. A stored hex cannot theme-switch, and dark is a full peer. Anything rendering a domain colour resolves it through var(--domain-<slug>).

rules.name: The Recorded Contrast Tradeoff
rules.body: ink-3 (3.3:1) and ink-4 (2.0:1) miss WCAG AA at 12px on paper. That is the pinned palette and a recorded decision — fidelity over the contrast floor. Do not "fix" it locally; reversing it is a darkening of two tokens, which lands on every surface at once.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: 400 and 500. There is no 600 and no bold. If something is not standing out enough, it needs to be bigger, in a different colour, or in the mono register — never heavier.

rules.name: The Named vs Labelled Rule
rules.body: If a person wrote it, it is sans. If the system labelled it, it is uppercase mono. A row's title is sans; the time beside it is mono. This is why the page reads as two columns of meaning without any rules being drawn.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change under the reader — a clock, a count, a streak, a percentage — is tabular-nums. Digits that reflow while you look at them are a defect.

rules.name: The Closed Ramp Rule
rules.body: 56/44/36/30/18/16/14/12, plus micro at 11px in three named sites. That is the whole ramp. A fourth 11px site, or any new size at all, is a signal that a layout is too dense — fix the layout, do not invent a step. If a new step is genuinely warranted, it lands in DESIGN.md first and in the code second.

rules.name: The One Tree Rule
rules.body: A phone layout is a max-width query beside its desktop peer, plus display: contents and order. If a <MobileX> component is being written, the layout is wrong.

rules.name: The Invisible Slot Rule
rules.body: A control that appears conditionally holds its slot with visibility, not display, so its neighbours never shift. The day nav's Today reset is the canonical case.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are cast in rgba(41,37,36,…), not in black. A neutral shadow on a warm ground reads as dirt.

rules.name: The Shape-Then-Colour Rule
rules.body: Shape distinguishes kinds; colour distinguishes instances. Colour is never the only thing separating two things that behave differently.

dos: Do use size, colour, or the mono register to create hierarchy. Weight is not available: the ramp stops at 500.
Do resolve a domain colour through var(--domain-<slug>) from the stored slug. Never write a domain hex into a component.
Do pair colour with a shape or a word whenever it carries meaning — an outlined tick versus a filled block, a 6d late label beside the orange.
Do hold a conditional control's slot with visibility so its neighbours never shift.
Do write a phone layout as a max-width query beside its desktop peer, and reorder with display: contents + order.
Do give every number that can change under the reader tabular-nums.
Do let an empty band say so in words. Absent, never empty; a placeholder, never a collapse.
Do cast shadows in rgba(41,37,36,…) on light.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent, or spend the orange on anything that is not "this needs you". Its rarity is the entire signal.
Don't retune a domain colour by hand. Change it in .impeccable/mocks/palette-lab.html, re-measure against the three floors, or leave it alone.
Don't "fix" the ink-3 / ink-4 contrast locally. It is a recorded tradeoff; reversing it is a change to two tokens in the theme.
Don't put a title inside a day-tape block. There is no width for it at either breakpoint, and the Timeline below already carries it.
Don't fork a component for the phone. If a <MobileX> is being written, the layout is wrong.
Don't spend the pill voice on ordinary controls. Two standing actions and the Today reset; everything else is the mono control.
Don't move anything on hover. Hover is a colour change.
Don't draw a ring at 0% for something with nothing to measure — that is furniture, not a reading.
